title: Is Apple Log HDR? Separate the Recording from Delivery
description: Identify Apple Log versus HLG HDR before converting an iPhone clip. Separate camera recording from SDR or HDR delivery and keep the original.
direct: Apple Log describes how the camera records a clip for color work. HDR can describe how a finished clip is delivered. An HLG tag alone does not identify Apple Log.
figureAlt: A Log recording card beside separate SDR and HDR delivery envelopes illustrates different stages of a color workflow.
figureCaption: AI-generated conceptual illustration, not an App screenshot or measured export. The envelopes show possible delivery goals in a color-managed workflow, not VideoFix HDR output.
cards.decision.heading: Appearance can mislead
cards.decision.body: A pale preview is a symptom, not an identification method. Applying an Apple Log transform to ordinary HLG footage because both look unfamiliar can introduce another color error.
sections.detail-0-0.heading: Recording and viewing are separate decisions
sections.detail-0-0.body: Apple’s Final Cut Camera guide separates standard, HDR, Log and RAW workflows. Log preserves a different starting representation for color work; the editor’s output settings determine the delivery. A normal-looking, color-managed preview does not prove that the source has already been permanently converted.
sections.detail-1-0.heading: Match the supported source
sections.detail-1-0.body: Its public listing supports Apple ProRes Log and HDR conversion into Rec.709 SDR, with three free conversions before a purchase is needed. It does not establish Apple Log 2, HEVC Log, arbitrary camera profiles or HDR output here.
sections.detail-1-1.heading: Keep the camera original
sections.detail-1-1.body: If source identification is uncertain, resolve it before batch conversion. Keep the camera original when you may want a different grade or HDR delivery later.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Can a Log clip be graded for HDR?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: Yes, in a suitable HDR workflow. Match the camera encoding to the editor’s color management. VideoFix’s workflow in this guide produces a Rec.709 SDR copy.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Does a flat-looking preview prove the clip is Log?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: No. Check the original recording mode or read the file’s color information. A wrong viewing transform can also produce an unfamiliar image.

steps.step-1.text: Check the camera recording setting and the original file’s color information in a trusted editor. Keep the original tags. A MOV extension or ProRes label alone does not identify the transfer function.
steps.step-2.text: For verified Apple ProRes Log that needs standard SDR delivery, use the supported Log-to-Rec.709 conversion in VideoFix: HDR Video Converter. For HDR input, use its HDR-to-SDR workflow instead.
steps.step-3.text: Inspect the saved H.264 MP4 in the intended SDR player. Check faces, highlights and shadows. Do not apply the same Log conversion again to an already converted Rec.709 copy.
